subject: marginals.fixed is always a df with 43 rows?

messages.author: 9c5355749af01ead
messages.subject: marginals.fixed is always a df with 43 rows?
parts: I'm making my head around the outputs of inla for Poisson (also ZIP) regressions and realized the marginals.fixed is always returning a df of 43 rows and 2 columns. My data has 462 spatial units so I am not sure where the 43 rows come from. I assessed this for another dataset with 450 spatial units (a complete different setting). The output of m$marginals.fixed[[1]] is again a df with 43 rows, 2 columns (for the x,y components). I am not sure if I am missing something here or I am making a mistake in the specification of the models? Sorry if the question is silly but I would appreciate any feedback. Best, Jac

messages.author: 9c5355749af01ead
messages.subject: Re: marginals.fixed is always a df with 43 rows?
parts: Just a correction, actually it is a 43x2 matrix (not a df). I would appreciate any advice/feedback on my question above.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: marginals.fixed is always a df with 43 rows?
parts:
The storage for "marginals.fixed" is a list of matrices containing the
estimated posterior density for each fixed effect in the model. The
two columns are x-values and density values at those x-values.

Finn
